title: Federal employees’ pay protest across Islamabad venues
location: Islamabad: Pakistan Secretariat, National Press Club, and Golra area
participants_original: Dawn reports more than 2,000 employees inside the Secretariat, over 1,000 at the National Press Club, and about 1,500–2,000 intercepted near Golra while arriving. These are site-specific figures that may overlap.
threshold_50_evidence: The report says more than 2,000 gathered inside the Secretariat, independently exceeding 50. Do not sum the other location estimates or assume they are distinct people.

start_date.summary: Dawn places the protest on Wednesday, February 10; February 11 is the article publication date.

location.summary: Dawn names the Secretariat, National Press Club, and Golra area; location estimates remain separate and may overlap.

organizer.summary: The protest is organized under the All Government Employees Grand Alliance.

demands.summary: Employees demanded salary increases matching prevailing inflation.

participants_original.summary: Dawn reports more than 2,000 at the Secretariat, over 1,000 at the Press Club, and about 1,500–2,000 intercepted at Golra; do not pool.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The Secretariat section alone is reported as more than 2,000 people.

protester_violence.summary: The report says employees pelted police with stones.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish physical departure or a protest end date.

state_response.summary: Police arrested union leaders and protesters, used tear gas to disperse the crowd, fired rubber bullets, and used batons at Golra. A government committee negotiated and an adjustment was offered subject to formal agreement. Other response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: A February 10 multivenue action, later than and physically separate from the January 12 D-Chowk protest. The three location estimates are not added together. PIMS employees’ separate strike/call-off is not part of this candidate.
open_questions: Verify any departure or physical end, and whether later coverage identifies separate local assemblies within the coordinated action.
Clarify the relation to the January pay protest as campaign recurrence only; do not infer continuous gathering.
Independent review and official baseline verification remain pending.

title: Baloch missing-persons families’ Islamabad sit-in ends after PM meeting assurance
location: Islamabad; exact sit-in site not named
organizer: Families of missing men from Balochistan; exact organization not named
participants_original: Reuters/Dawn reports 10 families and around 100 supporters.
threshold_50_evidence: The report’s estimate of around 100 supporters, in addition to 10 families, supports the 50-person threshold while remaining approximate.

start_date.summary: The report calls the sit-in week-long but does not state its exact start date.

end_date.summary: Reuters/Dawn says participants ended the sit-in on Monday, February 22, after a promise of a meeting with the Prime Minister the following month.

location.summary: The report locates the sit-in in Islamabad without naming its precise site.

organizer.summary: The article describes families of missing men from Balochistan and around 100 supporters; it does not name a formal organizing group.

demands.summary: Families were calling for an end to enforced disappearances in Balochistan.

participants_original.summary: The report describes 10 families and around 100 supporters; the figure is approximate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Around 100 supporters are reported, in addition to 10 families.

state_response.summary: The group ended the sit-in after assurance of a future meeting with the Prime Minister; police watched and surrounded the sit-in. No other response dimensions are reported.

notes: Use February 22 as the reported end date. No exact onset or site is reported. Do not merge with the separate Voicepk camp/march record PAK202102-E003 solely because the issue and city are similar.
open_questions: Seek the exact onset, site, and any additional event-specific state or participant conduct.
Check whether independent coverage establishes that this group is the same as the families described by PAK-S134; keep distinct pending corroboration.
Independent review and official baseline verification remain pending.

title: Missing-persons families’ Press Club camp and march to D-Chowk, Islamabad
location: Islamabad: outside the Press Club and D-Chowk
organizer: Families of missing Baloch people; other organizers not established
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance figure is supplied; whether the gathering reached 50 is unresolved.

start_date.summary: The retrospective article says the camp began about one week before a February 15 press conference, but elsewhere says five days; no exact onset date is established.

location.summary: Families camped outside the Islamabad Press Club and a planned February 16 march went to D-Chowk, where the article describes a sit-in.

organizer.summary: The article describes families of missing Baloch people; it does not establish a formal organizer for the camp or march.

demands.summary: Families sought recovery or release of missing relatives and meetings with the Prime Minister or Army Chief.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article provides no attendance figure or clear qualitative size.

state_response.summary: The article describes meetings with commission and Senate officials and promises of further meetings/visits. It does not establish fulfillment; other state-response dimensions are unknown.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish the camp or D-Chowk sit-in’s physical end.

notes: This is a distinct provisional record from PAK-S131. The Voicepk account is retrospective, repeats passages, and has an internally inconsistent camp-duration chronology. It establishes a February 16 planned march and reports the camp/sit-in, but not attendance or final departure.
open_questions: Seek a contemporaneous attendance estimate, exact onset, physical end, and response coverage.
Resolve whether this gathering and the February 22 Reuters/Dawn sit-in are the same people or separate actions before any episode merge.
Determine whether the group crossed the 50-person threshold.
Independent review and official baseline verification remain pending.

title: Islamabad lawyers protest CDA demolition of chambers at judicial complex
location: Islamabad judicial complex, including the IHC building
organizer: Islamabad lawyers; the specific coordinating bar body is not established
threshold_50_evidence: Geo gives no attendance figure or qualitative crowd size; the threshold is unresolved.

start_date.summary: Geo reports that lawyers protested on Monday, February 8, after the prior-night demolition of chambers.

location.summary: The report places the protest at the Islamabad judicial complex and IHC building.

organizer.summary: The report identifies protesting Islamabad lawyers but not a specific convening body.

demands.summary: Demands included rebuilding chambers and compensation, release of arrested colleagues, transfers of officials/judges, and interim chambers.

protester_violence.summary: Geo reports lawyers smashed windows in the Chief Justice block and describes a clash involving journalists.

state_response.summary: A judge invited lawyers to talk and negotiations involved judges and government officials. The article reports closed entrances/road and barred access but not force or dispersal against protesters; other responses are unknown.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish physical departure or the protest end.

notes: A contemporaneous body supports a protest against a state-agency demolition and reports negotiations, but does not report attendance or physical end. Demands for release of previously arrested colleagues do not establish event-linked arrests.
open_questions: Find attendance evidence and physical end.
Distinguish this February 8 protest from later lawyers’ strike/demo calls and other chamber-related actions; do not merge from shared issue alone.
Independent review and official baseline verification remain pending.

title: PTM rally commemorating Ibrahim Luni in Chamkani, Peshawar
organizer: Pashtun Tahafuz Movement and allied party leaders
threshold_50_evidence: The article gives no attendance count or qualitative size; the 50-person threshold is unresolved.

start_date.summary: The News says the rally took place Sunday, February 7; the article was published February 8.

location.summary: The planned venue was changed to the Motorway Northern bypass in Chamkani, Peshawar.

organizer.summary: The article attributes the rally to PTM and allied leaders.

demands.summary: The stated purpose was to mark the second anniversary of Ibrahim Luni’s death. The article reports remarks about peace and detention of peaceful activists but no specific policy demand.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The report does not describe crowd size.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not describe violence by rally participants.

state_response.summary: The article does not report a police or other state response to this rally; all response dimensions remain unknown.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish a physical end.

notes: Retain as a reported rally lead, not yet an eligible protest candidate: the report gives neither attendance nor a specific policy request. The overnight venue change followed an attempt by unidentified locals to disrupt the event; it is not attributed to state action.
open_questions: Find an attendance estimate and evidence of a specific demand directed at Pakistan’s government or policy.
Identify who attempted to disrupt the rally and whether any further event response is documented.
Independent review and official baseline verification remain pending.
